sections.title: Technical Architecture and Mutation Prediction
sections.content: Whole-slide computational pathology images exceed 100,000 by 100,000 pixels, preventing direct end-to-end convolutional training [cite_cite_3]. To address this, pre-training a Vision Transformer (ViT-H/14) on 1.2 billion tissue patches using DINOv2 self-distillation extracts rich patch embeddings [cite_3_b]. An attention-based multiple-instance learning (MIL) aggregator then processes slide-level bags, achieving an AUROC of 0.94 for colorectal carcinoma subtyping [cite_3_c]. Furthermore, self-supervised pathology foundation models accurately predict clinically actionable driver mutations directly from hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) histology slides [cite_cite_4]. On multi-center non-small-cell lung cancer cohorts, the model predicted EGFR mutation status with an AUROC of 0.86 and KRAS status with an AUROC of 0.83, without requiring prior stain normalization [cite_4_b].

executive_summary.title: Executive Summary
executive_summary.content: Self-supervised foundation models are transforming computational pathology by overcoming the massive dimensional challenges of whole-slide images and predicting molecular alterations directly from routine histology [cite_exec_1]. The models utilize advanced self-distillation and attention-based multiple-instance learning to achieve exceptional performance across cancer subtyping and genetic mutation prediction [cite_exec_2] [cite_exec_3].

sections.title: Technical Architecture and Mutation Prediction
sections.content: Whole-slide computational pathology images exceed 100,000 by 100,000 pixels, preventing direct end-to-end convolutional training [cite_cite_3]. To address this, pre-training a Vision Transformer (ViT-H/14) on 1.2 billion tissue patches using DINOv2 self-distillation extracts rich patch embeddings [cite_3_b]. An attention-based multiple-instance learning (MIL) aggregator then processes slide-level bags, achieving an AUROC of 0.94 for colorectal carcinoma subtyping [cite_3_c]. Furthermore, self-supervised pathology foundation models accurately predict clinically actionable driver mutations directly from hematoxylin and eosin (H&E) histology slides [cite_cite_4]. On multi-center non-small-cell lung cancer cohorts, the model predicted EGFR mutation status with an AUROC of 0.86 and KRAS status with an AUROC of 0.83, without requiring prior stain normalization [cite_4_b].
